task: M5.32 R23-1b adversarial audit (claims D1 to D9)
independence: no import from the record; energy, gradient, M_00 solve, seed, half-energy reader, degree reader, disclination counter and fit forms reused from the earlier independent auditor (m5_32_r23_1_audit.py); shells, r_eps reader and variants, rms radius, linear theory, k4, box integral, stability probe, label replica are new

checks.claim: every end field of the ladder exists, is block-diagonal and symmetric
checks.method: tags rebuilt from the claim text; max |M_0i| and max |S - S^T| over all cells
checks.expectation: no missing tag, M_0i exactly zero, asymmetry under 1e-15
checks.fails_if: a missing end field, a nonzero M_0i or an asymmetric spatial block

checks.claim: stored E, E_curv, V4, E_lin of every n48 row and of the two new n32 rows reproduce from the end fields
checks.method: the earlier auditor's energy code (one-sided stencils, per-cell potential) on the end field against the last chunk of the row whose E is nearest
checks.expectation: every relative difference under 1e-8
checks.fails_if: any energy part of any of the 11 rows off by 1e-8 relative or more

checks.claim: the stored fmax_spatial of the same 11 rows reproduces
checks.method: the earlier auditor's analytic gradient, max |G_ab| over free cells (2 pinned layers)
checks.expectation: relative difference under 1e-6 on every row
checks.fails_if: a stored fmax that my gradient does not reproduce to 1e-6

checks.claim: the outer shell is pinned at the analytic seed; its depth is 2 cells on every lattice (3.0 at h 1.5, 2.0 at h 1.0; the record's '1.6' is the nominal depth before rounding up)
checks.method: own seed against the end field on the 2 outer layers and on the first free layer
checks.expectation: pinned cells equal the seed to 1e-13 and the first free layer has moved
checks.fails_if: a pinned cell off the seed, or a first free layer still at the seed (a deeper pin)

checks.claim: the summary the record quotes (collect JSON) carries, for every row, the E of the end field on disk (one row exists twice in the row files)
checks.method: collect E against my E of the end field
checks.expectation: relative difference under 1e-8 on every row
checks.fails_if: a collect row quoting a chunk that is not the end field on disk

checks.claim: the stored eps profile of every row is the shell mean of (mid - small) / 2 on |r - R| < h / 2, R on the 0.75 grid up to L/2 - 2h
checks.method: own eigenvalues and own shells on the end field against the last chunk
checks.expectation: max abs difference under 1e-10 and the same number of points
checks.fails_if: a stored profile I cannot rebuild from the end field

checks.claim: the 16 quoted r_eps values (and the three None reads on n32 L48)
checks.method: own reader on own shell profile (half-width h / 2, the record's definition)
checks.expectation: each within 0.006 of the quote, None where the record says None
checks.fails_if: any value off by more than 0.006 or a None / number mismatch

checks.claim: the r_eps values inside the window c 3e-4 to 3e-3 are properties of the field, not of the shell definition (they are quoted to 4 figures)
checks.method: the same reader on shell means with half-width 0.75, h and 0.375 (the record uses h / 2); the shell median and the shell rms are listed too but do not enter the verdict
checks.expectation: every mean-shell variant within 5 percent of the quoted value
checks.fails_if: a shell width that moves a window value by 5 percent or more (that is 0.05 on a local slope over a factor 3 in c)

checks.claim: the r_eps values at the ceiling (c <= 1e-4, and n48 L48 c 3e-4) and at the floor (c >= 1e-2) are stable against the shell definition
checks.method: same as above
checks.expectation: every mean-shell variant within 5 percent and never None
checks.fails_if: a shell width that moves a value by 5 percent or more, or turns it into None (the read then sits on the end of the stored window)

checks.claim: the three None reads on n32 L48 mean 'beyond the stored window (r = 21)', not 'no halo'
checks.method: the weighted profile at the last stored radius, and the L72 read at the same c
checks.expectation: weighted profile still above one half at r = 21 and the L72 read above 21
checks.fails_if: a None row whose L72 read lies inside the L48 window

checks.claim: for c >= 1e-2 r_eps reads 6.3 to 7.6 and the interpolated half-energy radius 5.6 to 5.8
checks.method: own reads on the four end fields
checks.expectation: r_eps in [6.30, 7.65] and interpolated r_half in [5.55, 5.85] on all four rows
checks.fails_if: a read outside the quoted range

checks.claim: the top two ladder points carry no halo-size information: no size read still responds to c between 1e-2 and 3e-2
checks.method: local log slope between c 1e-2 and 3e-2 of five size reads on both spacings
checks.expectation: every |slope| under 0.1 (a -1/4 law would give -0.25)
checks.fails_if: a size read that still falls with a slope of magnitude 0.1 or more (the rows would then carry information and the floor would be the reader's, not the field's)

checks.claim: WORDING: 'the halo has retreated into the seed's core scale' (a halo of the same amplitude with a smaller radius)
checks.method: shell-mean eps at r = 4.5, 6, 9 at c = 3e-3 against c = 1e-2, both spacings; a retreating cutoff envelope bounds the drop at r = 4.5

largest_drop_at_r4.5_a_pure_retreat_allo.assumption: K_nu envelope exp(-r^2 / 2 R^2), R = 5.12 at c 3e-3 shrinking as c^(-1/2) (the steepest law on the table)

checks.expectation: eps(4.5) falls by less than 5 (twice the bound of a pure retreat)
checks.fails_if: eps at the core edge falls by 5 or more between c 3e-3 and 1e-2: the split does not shrink, its amplitude collapses (the halo is gone, not retreated)

checks.claim: the residual split at c >= 1e-2 is set by the core (a physical, spacing-independent profile), not by the lattice
checks.method: shell-mean eps (equal physical half-width 0.75) at r = 4.5, 6, 9 on L48 at h 1.5 against h 1.0; c = 3e-3 is the control where a real halo is present
checks.expectation: ratio h 1.5 / h 1.0 inside [0.8, 1.25] at c 1e-2 and 3e-2, as it is at the control
checks.fails_if: a ratio outside [0.8, 1.25] at c >= 1e-2: the residual eps scales with the spacing (about h^2 = 2.25), so it is discretization biaxiality of a uniaxial hedgehog

checks.claim: the almost uniaxial state at c = 1e-2 is a minimum, not a symmetric stationary point that the uniaxial seed never left
checks.method: own L-BFGS descent (own reduced energy and gradient, M_00 re-solved) from the n32 end field plus a biaxial core perturbation 0.05 exp(-(r/6)^2) diag(1, -1, 0)
checks.expectation: the descent returns: E not lower than the stored E by more than 1e-5 relative, and eps(6) within 10 percent of the stored field
checks.fails_if: a lower energy state with a larger split is found (the floor would be a seed artifact)

checks.claim: on n48 L72 the c = 3e-5 and 1e-4 reads are wall-limited and those rows are not converged (FALLING, fmax 5.0e-3 and 3.5e-3 against the gate 1e-3)
checks.method: r_eps against the free half-box (36 minus the 2 pinned layers = 33); the largest ratio demonstrated harmless is the L48 c = 1e-3 row (agrees with L72 to 2 percent)
checks.expectation: both reads above the demonstrated-safe ratio, both rows FALLING with fmax over gate
checks.fails_if: a read at or below the demonstrated-safe ratio (it would not be wall-limited by this evidence) or a row at the gate

checks.claim: inside the readable window (c >= 3e-4) the two boxes agree on eps(r) within 10 percent over 5 <= r <= 15 (same spacing 1.5, same shells)
checks.method: max over shells of |eps_L48 / eps_L72 - 1| per c, also on 5-12 and 5-21 and with wide shells
checks.expectation: under 10 percent at c = 3e-4, 1e-3 and 3e-3
checks.fails_if: a window c where the boxes differ by 10 percent or more on 5 <= r <= 15

checks.claim: on n48 L72 the local log slopes of r_eps are -0.27 and -0.49, those of the fitted K_nu cutoff (10.83, 7.67, 5.12) are -0.29 and -0.37
checks.method: own r_eps; the earlier auditor's log-space K_nu fit on my profile (5 <= r <= 30, eps above 1e-3 of its r = 5 value)
checks.expectation: slopes within 0.01 of the quotes, K_nu radii within 1 percent
checks.fails_if: a slope off by more than 0.01 or a K_nu radius off by more than 1 percent

checks.claim: the fitted K_nu cutoff is a read of the profile (it does not depend on whether the least squares run in log space or in linear space)
checks.method: the same two-parameter K_nu form fitted both ways on the same points
checks.expectation: the two radii within 15 percent on all three window rows, RMS log residual under 0.15
checks.fails_if: a row where the radius moves by 15 percent or more with the metric, or where the K_nu form misses the profile by more than 15 percent RMS (the 'cutoff' is then a property of the fit, and so are its slopes)

checks.claim: the K_nu cutoff agrees between the boxes where r_eps does (c = 1e-3 and 3e-3)
checks.method: K_nu log fit on both boxes; the L72 fit repeated on the L48 window (5 to 18) to separate the window from the box

n48_L72_window_5_to_18_at_c3e-4.note: above 400 means no cutoff inside r <= 18: the fit runs away

checks.expectation: L48 against L72 (each on its own window, as the record quotes them) within 10 percent
checks.fails_if: a K_nu cutoff that differs by 10 percent or more between boxes whose r_eps agree to 2 percent

checks.claim: inside the window the radius is not a power law of c: no size read gives one exponent
checks.method: two local slopes per read on n48 L72 (15 reads: r_eps with other reference radii, levels, weights and shells; the eps^2-weighted rms radius; the interpolated half-energy radius; the disclination network's outer radius; K_nu and Yukawa scales, the K_nu fit also on the linear tail alone and on the 5 to 18 window, which has no cutoff at c = 3e-4 and drops out)
checks.expectation: every read has local slopes differing by more than 0.10 (the 2 percent convergence uncertainty of a radius is 0.02 on a slope)
checks.fails_if: a read whose two local slopes agree within 0.10: that read cannot exclude a single exponent

checks.claim: WORDING: 'neither -1/4 nor -1/2 is certified and both lie inside the spread'
checks.method: the literal intervals spanned by the quoted slopes
checks.expectation: -0.25 and -0.5 inside [min, max] of the two quoted r_eps slopes
checks.fails_if: either exponent outside the interval of the quoted r_eps slopes (true only of the union over other reads, or within the 0.02 convergence uncertainty)

checks.claim: the readable window is c in [3e-4, 3e-3]: both end points are free of the floor and of structure in the read region
checks.method: upper end: r_eps against the floor value at the same spacing, and the split amplitude at r = 4.5 against the plateau; lower end: the outer radius of the disclination network against the start of the read region (r_ref 4.5, fit window from 5)
checks.expectation: r_eps(3e-3) at least twice the floor, eps(4.5) within 20 percent of its c = 3e-4 value, the network inside r = 5 on all three rows
checks.fails_if: an end point within a factor 2 of the floor, an amplitude already down by more than 20 percent, or a network reaching into the read region

checks.claim: the FALLING L72 rows at c = 3e-4 and 1e-3 (fmax 1.1e-3 and 6.7e-3) are converged enough for their radii
checks.method: r_eps recomputed from every stored chunk of the last 1000 iterations; the converged L48 row at c = 1e-3 as a cross-check
checks.expectation: change over the last 1000 iterations under 2 percent, last chunk step under 0.5 percent, L48 and L72 within 3 percent at c = 1e-3
checks.fails_if: a radius still moving by 2 percent per 1000 iterations or more

checks.claim: the L48 and L72 half-energy radii differ by 11.7 percent at c = 3e-5 and by 7.1 percent at c = 1e-4 (L72 row unconverged); the pre-registered label is HALO_BOX_LIMITED
checks.method: own half-energy radius (cell reader and interpolated) on the four end fields
checks.expectation: cell-reader differences within 0.002 of 0.117 and 0.071, label HALO_BOX_LIMITED
checks.fails_if: a difference I cannot reproduce or another label in the collect JSON

checks.claim: WORDING: HALO_BOX_LIMITED is a robust outcome of the pre-registered rule
checks.method: replica of the rule's last step from the collect summary: the c = 1e-4 box check passes its 10 percent gate (7.1) and is excluded only by the drift flag of the L72 row (r_half drift 2.35 percent against 2.0, read on a cell-quantized radius); the label the rule gives if that one flag flips
checks.expectation: the same label HALO_BOX_LIMITED
checks.fails_if: another label: the outcome then hangs on a 0.35 point margin of one drift read, and the alternative label would rest on a fit through the floor rows c >= 1e-2

checks.claim: the linearized one-mode equation predicts r_eps = 18.5, 14.0, 11.0, 8.6, 7.2; the L72 reads are 1.3 to 2.0 times larger; a factor 2 in R is a factor 16 in beta
checks.method: the record's reader on sqrt(r) K_nu(sqrt(beta) r^2 / 2), beta = 5.81 c / (2 * 3.92), on the reader's 0.75 grid and on a 0.001 grid
checks.expectation: predictions within 0.05 of the quotes; ratio range within 0.05 of [1.3, 2.0]
checks.fails_if: a prediction or a ratio I cannot reproduce

checks.claim: possible reason 1 is absent: in the read region the split is small enough for the linearized potential term (5.81 c eps^2 dominates V4 = k4 eps^4)
checks.method: k4 from my own per-cell potential on the split with M_00 re-solved; eps_x = sqrt(5.81 c / (2 k4)) is where the two restoring forces are equal; shell-mean eps at r = 6
checks.expectation: force ratio (eps / eps_x)^2 at r = 6 under 0.25 at every c of the five
checks.fails_if: a c where the quartic V4 force at r = 6 is a quarter of the linear one or more: the linear equation cannot hold from r_ref on, and nonlinearity is a live reason for the prefactor

checks.claim: possible reason 2 is absent: the disclination network of the top eigenvector stays inside the read region's inner edge (r_ref 4.5, fit window from 5)
checks.method: frustrated elementary squares over the free region (the earlier auditor's counter), their largest radius
checks.expectation: r_max under 5 at every c of the five
checks.fails_if: a c where the network reaches r = 5 or beyond (the one-mode, defect-free ansatz is then not the state that was measured)

checks.claim: 'the linearized one-mode equation does not describe the measured halo quantitatively' survives a fairer test: the K_nu cutoff fitted ONLY on the linear tail (eps below half of eps_x) against beta^(-1/4)
checks.method: log-space K_nu fit restricted to shells with eps < eps_x / 2, r >= 5; ratio of the fitted cutoff to the theoretical one
checks.expectation: the record's statement stands: at least one ratio outside [0.9, 1.1]
checks.fails_if: every tail ratio inside [0.9, 1.1]: the equation would then describe the tail and the factor 1.3 to 2.0 would be the r_eps reader starting inside the nonlinear plateau

checks.claim: at c = 3e-3: r_eps 9.36, 9.39, 8.82 and E 6.2314, 6.5104, 6.3330; the L48 to L72 energy difference is 0.279 (4.5 percent)
checks.method: own reads and own energies
checks.expectation: r_eps within 0.006, E within 1e-4, difference within 0.001 of 0.279
checks.fails_if: any quoted number off

checks.claim: the curvature energy density of the uniaxial hedgehog is 8 (1 - delta)^4 / r^4
checks.method: the earlier auditor's lattice curvature density on S = delta I + (1 - delta) rhat rhat^T, mean of density r^4 / (1 - delta)^4 over cells with 10 < r < 18 at h = 1.5
checks.expectation: coefficient within 3 percent of 8
checks.fails_if: a lattice coefficient off 8 by more than 3 percent

checks.claim: the 0.279 energy difference between L48 and L72 at c = 3e-3 is the Coulomb tail of the hedgehog between the two walls
checks.method: lattice hedgehog curvature energy outside r = 12 on each lattice (boundary stencils and pinned shells as the rows have them), L72 minus L48; the continuum cube-minus-cube integral; the rows' own difference split inside / outside r = 12
checks.expectation: the hedgehog difference within 5 percent of 0.279 and the rows' difference inside r = 12 under 5 percent of 0.279
checks.fails_if: a hedgehog tail that misses 0.279 by more than 5 percent, or an interior that differs between the boxes by more than 0.014

checks.claim: clean unit |degree| with zero orientation conflicts on the r 6, 9, 12 cubes for every rad-seed row with c >= 1e-3 on every box and spacing
checks.method: the earlier auditor's reader (gauge-invariant frustrated squares, flood-fill orientation, solid-angle degree) on the record's cube and on the box-centered cube
checks.expectation: zero frustrated squares, zero conflicts, |degree| = 1 to 1e-6 on both cubes, 9 rows
checks.fails_if: a frustrated square, a conflict or a non-unit degree on any cube of a c >= 1e-3 row

checks.claim: conflicts appear only at c <= 3e-4, and every row there has them; the stored zero / nonzero pattern is the gauge-invariant one
checks.method: disclination piercings per cube on all 18 rows (values in D8.clean_degree_high_c)
checks.expectation: every c <= 3e-4 row pierced on at least one cube; stored conflicts zero exactly where my piercing count is zero
checks.fails_if: a clean c <= 3e-4 row, or a stored clean cube with piercings (or the reverse)

checks.claim: WORDING: the clean / pierced class of a cube does not depend on the record's cube being centered half a cell off the box center
checks.method: the same read on the box-centered cube (one cell wider on the low side)
checks.expectation: no cube changes class
checks.fails_if: a cube pierced on the record's cube and clean on the box-centered one, or the reverse

checks.claim: WORDING: the c ladder is one family of states (the disclination network shrinks smoothly with c, like the halo radius)
checks.method: outer radius of the network per row; the largest local log slope between neighbors
checks.expectation: local slope of the network radius between c 3e-4 and 1e-3 no steeper than -0.6
checks.fails_if: a slope steeper than -0.6 between two window points: the network collapses into the core between them, so the window straddles a structural change

checks.claim: V_0 = 0.019253, c_phys = 5.1e-6; anchored at r_eps(1e-3) = 16.1 the slopes -1/4 and -1/2 give 60 and 225 lattice units, 15 and 56 core radii
checks.method: own V4 of the isotropic block at M_00 = g; the conversion as stated
checks.expectation: V_0 within 1e-6, c_phys within 0.05e-6 of 5.1e-6, 60 and 225 within 1, 15 and 56 within 0.5
checks.fails_if: any of the quoted numbers off

checks.claim: WORDING: '15 to 56 core radii' is a fair statement of the extrapolation range
checks.method: the same two exponents anchored at each of the three window points, with r_eps and with the K_nu cutoff
checks.expectation: both ends of the range move by less than 20 percent under the anchor and the reader
checks.fails_if: an end of the range that moves by 20 percent or more (the range then states the anchor, not the extrapolation)

checks.claim: all extrapolated radii lie far outside both boxes, so nothing at the physical point was measured
checks.method: the smallest extrapolated radius over all anchors and readers against the larger free half-box (33)

value.note: the K_nu anchors give 25 to 30 lattice units, inside the L72 box; a cutoff radius is not an r_eps (r_eps is about 2 cutoff radii), so this does not put the physical point in reach, but 'all far outside both boxes' holds for r_eps only

checks.expectation: every r_eps extrapolation above 33
checks.fails_if: an r_eps extrapolation that fits inside the L72 free region
